home.title: Why compress images online
home.text1: Image compression shrinks a file's size without a noticeable drop in quality: photos load faster, your site ranks better in Google, and email attachments no longer clog up inboxes. The compressor runs right in your browser — JPG, PNG or WebP files are compressed in seconds, and the originals never leave your device.
home.text2: This matters most for website owners, bloggers and online stores: lighter images speed up page loads, improve Core Web Vitals, and directly affect search rankings. Smaller files also save disk space and are faster to send over messengers and email.

benefits.title: Speed
benefits.text: Compression happens instantly right in the browser — no queues or server upload waiting.

benefits.title: Privacy
benefits.text: Files are processed locally on your device and never uploaded to third-party servers.

benefits.title: Quality preserved
benefits.text: A smart algorithm shrinks file size while keeping the image sharp and colorful.

benefits.title: Works everywhere
benefits.text: The tool works equally well on desktop, tablet and phone — no software to install.

faq.q: How much smaller will my photo be after compression?
faq.a: Depending on the format and original quality, file size typically drops by 50-90% with almost no visible difference.

faq.q: Can I compress several photos at once?
faq.a: Yes, you can upload multiple images at once — each is processed and you can download the results as a single archive.

faq.q: Will the image quality drop?
faq.a: The algorithm picks an optimal compression level so the image still looks sharp even with a much smaller file size.

faq.q: Do I need to install any software?
faq.a: No, everything works right in the browser on any device — Windows, macOS, Android or iOS.

convert.title: Why convert images to JPG
convert.text1: JPG is one of the most widely supported image formats, compatible with websites, social networks, messaging apps, software and most devices. Converting PNG, WebP, HEIC and other formats to JPG helps prepare photos for services that require or work best with JPG.
convert.text2: Our JPG converter automatically optimizes the output settings for a strong balance between file size and visual quality. Convert multiple images at once and prepare photos from your phone, camera or computer in just a few clicks.

benefits.title: Widely supported
benefits.text: JPG works across websites, devices, image editors and online services.

benefits.title: Automatic optimization
benefits.text: Output settings are adjusted automatically for an excellent balance of image quality and file size.

benefits.title: HEIC to JPG
benefits.text: Convert iPhone photos from HEIC or HEIF to JPG directly in your browser.

benefits.title: Batch conversion
benefits.text: Upload multiple images and convert them at the same time.

faq.q: Which formats can I convert to JPG?
faq.a: Popular formats such as PNG, WebP, HEIC, HEIF and BMP are supported.

faq.q: Will my photo stay high quality after conversion?
faq.a: Yes. The converter automatically selects suitable JPG settings to provide high visual quality in the final file.

faq.q: Can I convert iPhone photos?
faq.a: Yes. HEIC and HEIF photos can be converted to JPG directly in your browser.

faq.q: Can I convert multiple photos at once?
faq.a: Yes. Upload multiple images and process them together.

resize.title: Why resize a photo
resize.text1: Resizing an image is needed when a photo is too large for a website upload, a form with specific size requirements, or a social network with a fixed post format. Instead of guessing proportions by hand, the tool lets you set an exact width and height or pick a ready-made preset.
resize.text2: The right image size saves visitors' bandwidth, speeds up page loading, and improves Google PageSpeed scores. For social media, it also guarantees the photo won't be cropped awkwardly in a feed or profile.

benefits.title: Ready-made presets
benefits.text: Sizes for Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and Twitter are set up in advance — just pick the platform.

benefits.title: Crop control
benefits.text: Manually choose which part of the photo to keep when changing proportions by dragging the crop area.

benefits.title: Aspect ratio lock
benefits.text: The fixed aspect ratio option prevents distortion when only one side is changed.

benefits.title: Output format choice
benefits.text: Save the resized photo as JPG, PNG or WebP, depending on where it will be used.

faq.q: How do I resize a photo for a specific social network?
faq.a: Pick a ready preset (Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, Twitter) and the dimensions are applied automatically.

faq.q: What if the new proportions don't match the original?
faq.a: The tool offers cropping, and you can drag the crop area to choose which part of the photo to keep.

faq.q: Can I set only the width and have the height calculated automatically?
faq.a: Yes, aspect ratio lock is on by default — just enter one value.

faq.q: What format is the result saved in?
faq.a: You can choose JPG, PNG or WebP right before downloading the finished file.

webp.title: Why convert photos to WebP
webp.text1: WebP is a modern image format from Google that compresses photos far more efficiently than JPG or PNG while keeping almost the same visual quality. Google officially recommends WebP for websites, since lighter images directly affect page load speed and search rankings.
webp.text2: WebP supports modern image features, including transparency, and can be used as a compact format for websites and web applications.

benefits.title: Smaller file size
benefits.text: WebP is typically 25-35% lighter than a JPG of the same visual quality.

benefits.title: Better SEO
benefits.text: Lighter images speed up your site, which positively affects Core Web Vitals and Google rankings.

benefits.title: Transparency support
benefits.text: Unlike JPG, WebP supports an alpha channel — convert logos and icons without a white background.

benefits.title: Wide compatibility
benefits.text: The format is supported by every modern browser and most CMS platforms.

faq.q: Why is WebP better than JPG for a website?
faq.a: WebP gives a smaller file size at the same quality, which speeds up page loads and improves SEO metrics.

faq.q: Do all browsers support WebP?
faq.a: Yes, all modern versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge display WebP without extra settings.

faq.q: Can I convert iPhone HEIC photos to WebP?
faq.a: Yes, HEIC and HEIF files are supported alongside JPG, PNG and BMP.

faq.q: Is background transparency lost when converting to WebP?
faq.a: No, WebP supports transparency, so logos and PNGs with a transparent background convert correctly.

presets.title: Why use photo presets
presets.text1: Presets are ready-made sets of color, contrast and tone adjustments that give photos a finished, stylish look in one click. Instead of manually editing every image in a complex photo editor, just pick a category (portrait, nature, urban, night) and apply the filter.
presets.text2: A consistent editing style across all your photos creates a recognizable visual brand for a blog, online store or social media account. Each preset's intensity can be smoothly adjusted with a slider so the effect looks natural instead of overpowering the photo.

benefits.title: Ready-made categories
benefits.text: Filters are grouped by theme: portrait, nature, urban, night, summer, auto, cinematic, autumn, winter.

benefits.title: Adjustable intensity
benefits.text: The effect strength can be smoothly changed from 0% to 200% to find the perfect balance.

benefits.title: Before/after comparison
benefits.text: A before/after slider lets you clearly see how the preset changes the original photo.

benefits.title: Instant results
benefits.text: Processing happens instantly in the browser — the finished photo can be downloaded right away in high quality.

faq.q: What is a photo preset?
faq.a: It's a ready-made set of color and tone adjustments applied to a photo in one click instead of manual editing.

faq.q: Can I change the strength of a preset's effect?
faq.a: Yes, the intensity slider lets you reduce or boost the effect from 0% to 200%.

faq.q: Does image quality drop after applying a preset?
faq.a: No, the finished image is exported at high resolution with no extra compression.

faq.q: How many presets are available?
faq.a: Dozens of presets are available across categories: portrait, nature, urban, night, summer, auto, cinematic, autumn and winter.

wordToPdf.title: Why convert Word to PDF
wordToPdf.text1: PDF keeps a document's layout unchanged on any device — fonts, spacing and images look identical on a computer, a phone, or when printed. This matters for resumes, contracts, business proposals and official documents that shouldn't shift out of place when opened in a different version of Word.
wordToPdf.text2: A PDF file is also harder to accidentally alter than a .doc or .docx, which is why the format is the standard for sending final versions of documents. The file is sent over an encrypted connection to a conversion server and is automatically deleted from it after a short time; formatting, tables and images are preserved.

benefits.title: Formatting preserved
benefits.text: Fonts, spacing, tables and images look identical to the original on any device.

benefits.title: Ready to send
benefits.text: PDF opens without Word or LibreOffice — any viewer or browser is enough.

benefits.title: Batch conversion
benefits.text: Upload several .doc or .docx files at once and get all the PDFs as a single archive.

benefits.title: Harder to edit by accident
benefits.text: Unlike Word, a PDF document is less likely to be accidentally edited after it's sent.

faq.q: Is formatting preserved when converting Word to PDF?
faq.a: Yes, fonts, tables, images and spacing carry over to the PDF unchanged.

faq.q: Which document formats are supported?
faq.a: .doc and .docx files from any version of Microsoft Word or a compatible editor are accepted.

faq.q: Can I convert several documents at once?
faq.a: Yes, you can upload up to 10 files at a time and get the result as a single archive.

faq.q: Do I need Word installed to convert?
faq.a: No, the conversion happens on the service's server — no Word or other software is needed on your device.

pdfToWord.title: Why convert PDF to Word
pdfToWord.text1: PDF is great for viewing and printing but awkward to edit — fixing the text requires a .docx file that opens in Word or Google Docs. Converting PDF to Word restores the ability to edit text, tables and document structure without retyping everything by hand.
pdfToWord.text2: This is especially useful when working with old contracts, reports or forms where the original Word file has long been lost and only a scan or PDF version remains. The resulting .docx file keeps the paragraph structure and basic formatting of the original.

benefits.title: Editable result
benefits.text: The resulting .docx file can be opened and edited right away in Word or Google Docs.

benefits.title: Structure preserved
benefits.text: Paragraphs, headings and basic formatting carry over from PDF to Word as accurately as possible.

benefits.title: No manual retyping
benefits.text: There's no need to manually retype the text from the document — the converter does it automatically.

benefits.title: Batch processing
benefits.text: Upload several PDF files at once and get all the .docx files as a single archive.

faq.q: Can I edit the text after converting PDF to Word?
faq.a: Yes, the result is a regular .docx file that opens and can be edited in Word or Google Docs.

faq.q: Are scanned PDFs supported?
faq.a: The converter works best with text-based PDFs; for scans, we recommend using a text recognition (OCR) tool.

faq.q: Are tables and images preserved?
faq.a: The document's basic structure, including paragraphs and images, carries over to the Word file.

faq.q: How many files can I convert at once?
faq.a: You can upload up to 10 PDF files at the same time.

removeBg.title: Why remove the background from a photo
removeBg.text1: Background removal is needed for online store product photos, avatars, presentations or collages, when only the subject matters and not what's around it. Instead of cutting it out by hand in Photoshop, a neural network automatically detects the object's edges and removes the background in seconds.
removeBg.text2: The resulting image with a transparent background (PNG) can be placed on any other background, banner or layout without white or gray edges around the subject. A built-in magic brush lets you manually fix details the model may have removed or kept by mistake.

benefits.title: Automatic detection
benefits.text: A neural network identifies the object's edges in the photo on its own — no need to trace the outline by hand.

benefits.title: Magic brush
benefits.text: Manually restore or erase mask details — useful for hair, transparent edges or complex shapes.

benefits.title: Transparent PNG
benefits.text: The result is saved with an alpha channel, so the subject can easily be placed on another background.

benefits.title: Processed in the browser
benefits.text: The photo isn't uploaded to a third-party server — all processing happens locally on your device.

faq.q: Is this tool suitable for removing the background from product photos?
faq.a: Yes, that's one of its main use cases — product cards for marketplaces and online stores.

faq.q: What if the background isn't removed perfectly?
faq.a: Use the magic brush to manually restore or erase the parts of the mask you need.

faq.q: What format is the result saved in?
faq.a: The file is saved as PNG with a transparent background (alpha channel).

faq.q: Is the photo sent to a server for processing?
faq.a: No, background detection and removal happens right in your browser on your device.

imageToText.title: Why recognize text from an image
imageToText.text1: Text recognition (OCR) turns text in a screenshot, scan or photo of a document into editable text that can be copied, edited or pasted into another document. It saves you from manually retyping quotes from books, documents, signs or presentation slides.
imageToText.text2: The tool works right in the browser without uploading images to third-party servers, which matters for confidential documents. The recognized text can be downloaded in a convenient format for further editing or archiving.

benefits.title: Fast recognition
benefits.text: Text in a photo or scan is recognized in seconds, with no manual retyping.

benefits.title: Multiple files at once
benefits.text: Upload up to 20 images at a time and recognize the text in each one.

benefits.title: Privacy
benefits.text: Recognition happens locally in the browser — images are never sent to a server.

benefits.title: Output format choice
benefits.text: The result can be saved in a convenient text format for further editing.

faq.q: Which images are supported for text recognition?
faq.a: JPG, PNG, WebP and BMP files are accepted — screenshots, photos of documents or scans.

faq.q: Is the image sent to a server?
faq.a: No, text recognition happens entirely in the browser on your device.

faq.q: How accurate is handwritten text recognition?
faq.a: Best results are achieved with printed text; handwritten text is recognized with lower accuracy.

faq.q: How many files can I process at once?
faq.a: You can upload up to 20 images at a time, each processed individually.

compressToSize.title: Why compress a photo to an exact size
compressToSize.text1: Many application forms, online accounts, mail services and classified-ad sites accept a photo only up to a certain size — 200 KB, for example. Ordinary compression doesn't help here: you can't tell how large the result will be, so you end up guessing where to put a quality slider. This tool works the other way round. You set the limit, and it finds the quality — and, if needed, the resolution — that keeps the file within it.
compressToSize.text2: Everything happens in your browser: the photo is not uploaded to a server, so it is fine for a scanned document or a passport-style picture as well. The result is saved as JPEG or WebP, and for every file you see the size before and after, the quality that was used and the final resolution.

benefits.title: Exactly within the limit
benefits.text: Enter a number in KB or MB — the file will not exceed it, and the quality will be the highest that fits.

benefits.title: No server upload
benefits.text: Files never leave your device, and no sign-up is needed.

benefits.title: An honest result
benefits.text: You see before → after, the quality and the resolution. If the target can't be reached, we say so plainly.

benefits.title: Several photos at once
benefits.text: Up to 20 photos at a time with the same limit; several files download as one ZIP archive.

sections.title: How to compress a photo to the size you need
steps: Choose the target size: click one of the presets (50, 100, 200, 500 or 1000 KB) or type your own number and pick KB or MB.
Pick the output format. JPEG is accepted almost everywhere; WebP usually gives a smaller file at the same quality but is not supported by every service.
Drop your photos into the upload area or click it to choose files. JPG, PNG, WebP, BMP and iPhone HEIC are supported.
Wait until it finishes: for each file the tool shows which quality it is currently trying.
Check the size and resolution in the list and download the result — a single file, or a ZIP archive if you added several photos.

sections.title: How the size is found
sections.text: The tool first tries a high quality, 95%. If the file is larger than the target, it checks the lower bound, 30%, and then uses a binary search to find the highest quality at which the file still fits; for one resolution that is at most eight attempts. If even 30% is not enough, the resolution is reduced in steps of 85%, but never below 600 pixels on the longer side. That way you get the largest resolution and the highest quality that fit the limit, instead of a file that was shrunk "just in case". Sizes are counted in thousands of bytes (1 KB = 1000 bytes), so the file fits the limit however your service counts.

sections.title: When you need it
sections.text: Photos for online application forms and personal accounts, job applications and CVs, e-mails with an attachment limit, forums, classified ads and CRM systems that refuse large files. It also helps when you need to quickly reduce the weight of a picture for a messenger or a website and you know exactly how much it is allowed to weigh.

sections.title: Limitations worth knowing
sections.text: A very small limit for a large, detailed photo can't be met without a visible loss of sharpness. If compressing to the size you asked for is impossible even at a resolution of 600 pixels, we will not hand you a ruined file — we will show the smallest size we managed to reach. Transparency is not kept: transparent areas of a PNG become white. Metadata (such as the date a photo was taken or its location) and the embedded colour profile are not carried into the result. If a JPG, PNG or WebP file is already not larger than the target, it is returned unchanged. A single file may be up to 30 MB, and up to 20 files can be processed at a time. Speed depends on your device: large pictures take longer on a slow phone.

sections.title: Privacy
sections.text: Compression runs locally in your browser, using your own device. Files are not sent to a server, are not stored and are not available to us. The page works without sign-up, and the contents of your photos are not passed to any analytics service.

faq.q: How do I compress an image to 200 KB?
faq.a: Choose 200 KB among the presets, add your photo and download the result. The tool picks the quality itself and, if necessary, lowers the resolution a little.

faq.q: Can I compress a photo to 100 KB without losing quality?
faq.a: Not entirely without loss — JPEG and WebP are lossy formats. We look for the highest quality at which the file fits the limit. For simple images the difference is barely visible, while very detailed photos will show artifacts at a small limit.

faq.q: What happens if the photo is already smaller than the limit?
faq.a: If a JPG, PNG or WebP file is already not larger than the target, we return it unchanged and tell you so — needless compression would only lower the quality.

faq.q: Why can't my photo be compressed to the size I need?
faq.a: Sometimes the target is too small for that picture. We lower the quality to 30% and the resolution down to 600 pixels on the longer side, and then stop. You will see the smallest size that was reached — choose a larger limit or a simpler image.

faq.q: Can I compress an iPhone photo in HEIC format?
faq.a: Yes, HEIC is recognised and converted to JPEG or WebP. The extra module needed for it is loaded only on this page, and only when you add a HEIC file.

faq.q: Is it safe to use this for photos of documents?
faq.a: Files never leave your device: processing happens in the browser. We can't see or store your photos.

convertToPng.title: Why convert an image to PNG
convertToPng.text1: PNG is a lossless format with true transparency. It is the one people ask for when it comes to logos, screenshots, diagrams, graphics for websites and presentations, and mockups in design tools. Often, though, the image reaches you in a different shape: a WebP saved from a browser, an iPhone HEIC, an AVIF from a modern website or a GIF. This page quickly turns such files into a PNG that opens anywhere.
convertToPng.text2: The conversion runs in your browser: files are not uploaded to a server, so personal photos and work material are both fine. The size in pixels stays the same, the rotation stored in the file is applied, and transparent areas are not filled in. Several images can be converted at once and download as a single ZIP archive.

benefits.title: Transparency is kept
benefits.text: If a WebP, AVIF or GIF had transparent areas, they stay transparent in the PNG instead of turning black or white.

benefits.title: No server upload
benefits.text: Everything happens on your device. No sign-up is needed.

benefits.title: Correct rotation
benefits.text: A phone photo does not end up lying on its side: the orientation stored in the file is applied.

benefits.title: Many formats and files
benefits.text: JPG, WebP, BMP, GIF, AVIF, HEIC and HEIF; up to 20 files at a time, several results in one ZIP.

sections.title: How to convert an image to PNG
steps: Drop your files into the upload area or click it and choose images. JPG, WebP, BMP, GIF, AVIF and iPhone HEIC are supported.
Wait a few seconds — each file is processed separately, and you can see what is happening to it.
Check the size before and after in the list: a PNG is often larger, and that is normal.
Download the result — a single PNG, or a ZIP archive if you added several files.

sections.title: PNG or JPG: which to choose
sections.text: PNG compresses an image without loss, which makes it a good fit for screenshots, logos, diagrams, interfaces and anything with crisp text, sharp edges or a transparent background. Ordinary photographs are a different story: as PNG they are usually noticeably heavier than as JPG or WebP, because they are full of smooth colour transitions. If you are preparing a photo for a website, an e-mail or a messenger and weight matters, keep JPG or WebP, and pick PNG when you need transparency or pixel-exact accuracy. Converting a JPG to PNG does not bring back detail that was already lost when the JPG was compressed: the artifacts stay, but from then on you can edit and re-save the file without losing quality a second time.

sections.title: About transparency
sections.text: WebP, AVIF and GIF can contain transparent areas, and a PNG keeps them. JPG and ordinary BMP have no transparency, so the PNG made from them will not have a transparent background either: wherever the original had a colour, it stays. If you need to remove the background from a photo, the site has a separate background-removal tool for that.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.text: For an animated GIF or WebP only the first frame is taken. Photo metadata, including EXIF and GPS coordinates, is not carried over into the PNG. HEIC files can become very large once turned into PNG. The limit is 30 MB per file and 20 files at a time; very large images on weak phones may fail to process, and you will see a message about it. If an AVIF file does not open, your browser does not support that format.

sections.title: Privacy
sections.text: The conversion runs locally in your browser, using your own device. Files are not sent to a server, are not stored and are not available to us. The page works without sign-up.

faq.q: Will PNG make my photo smaller?
faq.a: Mostly not. PNG stores the image without loss, so photographs in it are usually heavier than as JPG or WebP. To reduce the weight, keep JPG or WebP or use compression.

faq.q: Will the background become transparent when I convert a JPG to PNG?
faq.a: No. JPG has no transparency, so the background colour stays the same in the PNG. Making it transparent takes separate processing — background removal.

faq.q: Is quality lost during conversion?
faq.a: The move to PNG itself loses nothing: the pixel data is preserved exactly. But if the original was a compressed JPG or WebP, its losses were already in the file, and PNG cannot repair them.

faq.q: Can I convert an iPhone HEIC to PNG?
faq.a: Yes. Add a .heic or .heif file — the page recognises it and converts it. Keep in mind that a PNG made from such a photo can be very large.

faq.q: What happens to a GIF animation?
faq.a: Only the first frame is saved, as an ordinary PNG. This page does not preserve animation.

faq.q: Does the PNG contain the location where the photo was taken?
faq.a: No. Metadata, including EXIF and GPS, is not carried over into the PNG. But if your goal is specifically to strip metadata from a photo, a dedicated tool is the better choice.

removeExif.title: Why remove EXIF and metadata from photos
removeExif.text1: Every photo from a smartphone or a camera carries more than you can see on the screen. The file records the camera model, the date and time it was taken, lens settings, sometimes the device's serial number, the author's name and the name of the program used to edit the photo. The most sensitive part is the GPS coordinates: they show where exactly the picture was taken, including your home or workplace. This data is called metadata, and its most common format is EXIF.
removeExif.text2: This page shows what was found in each photo — camera, date, coordinates, software, author — and removes the metadata in one step. Everything happens in your browser: files are not uploaded to a server. For JPEG, PNG and WebP the pixel data is not re-encoded, so quality does not change.

benefits.title: See what was in the file
benefits.text: Camera, date taken, software, author, serial number and — as a separate warning — GPS coordinates.

benefits.title: No loss of quality
benefits.text: Only the auxiliary blocks are cut out of the file; the image itself stays byte for byte the same.

benefits.title: No server upload
benefits.text: Files never leave your device and no sign-up is needed.

benefits.title: JPEG, PNG and WebP
benefits.text: Up to 20 files at a time; several results download as one ZIP archive.

sections.title: How to remove metadata from a photo
steps: Drop your photos into the upload area or click it and choose files. JPEG, PNG and WebP are supported.
Wait a moment: for each file you get a summary — what was found and what was removed, including GPS coordinates if there were any.
Check the size before and after and download the result — a single file or a ZIP archive. Cleaned files get a "-clean" suffix in their name.

sections.title: What exactly is removed
sections.text: From a JPEG the tool removes the EXIF blocks (camera, date, settings, GPS, the embedded thumbnail), XMP, IPTC and other Photoshop data, comments, and everything written after the end of the image — for example the extra pictures some phones store inside the file. From a PNG it removes text fields, EXIF data and the modification time, and from a WebP the EXIF and XMP blocks. The embedded colour profile (ICC) is kept so the colours do not change.

sections.title: How it works without losing quality
sections.text: The usual way to "clean" a photo is to open it and save it again, and every such save slightly damages a JPEG. This works differently: the file is split into blocks, the metadata blocks are cut out, and the compressed image data is copied unchanged. That is why the pixels before and after match exactly.

sections.title: The rotation tag and the re-encoding mode
sections.text: Most portrait photos from smartphones are stored lying on their side, and a special rotation tag in EXIF tells viewers how to show them correctly. If it is deleted together with the rest, the photo opens sideways. So by default we keep only that tag in a JPEG — there is nothing personal in it. If you need to remove absolutely everything, turn on full re-encoding: the photo is physically rotated and the tag disappears. The price is that JPEG and WebP are saved again at 92% quality and the original colour profile is replaced with standard sRGB (the colours are recalculated, not lost).

sections.title: Limitations worth knowing
sections.text: Removing metadata is not anonymity. Faces, signs, car plates and landmarks remain in the picture itself, and the file name may contain a date or a place. HEIC is not supported: convert such photos to JPG first. The limit is 30 MB per file and 20 files at a time. Extra pictures that phones store after the main one (depth, an HDR map) are removed together with the other data, so on HDR displays the photo may look slightly different. Animated PNG and WebP can only be cleaned without re-encoding — otherwise only the first frame would be saved.

sections.title: Privacy
sections.text: Processing happens locally in your browser. Files are not sent to a server, are not stored and are not available to us. The library that reads the metadata is loaded only on this page and runs on your own device.

faq.q: Does removing EXIF reduce the quality of the photo?
faq.a: No. The image is not re-encoded: only auxiliary blocks are cut out of the file and the compressed pixel data stays the same. Quality changes only if you turn on full re-encoding yourself.

faq.q: Can the removed metadata be recovered?
faq.a: Not from the cleaned file: the blocks are not hidden, they are physically absent from the new file. You still have the original, so if you may need that data, keep it separately.

faq.q: What exactly is removed from a photo?
faq.a: EXIF (camera, date, settings, GPS coordinates, thumbnail), XMP, IPTC, comments and PNG text fields. The ICC colour profile is kept.

faq.q: Do social networks and messengers strip metadata by themselves?
faq.a: Some services remove metadata when you publish, but not all of them and not always: when a photo is sent as a file, by e-mail or to cloud storage, the data usually stays. It is safer to clean the file yourself before sending it.

faq.q: Which formats are supported?
faq.a: JPEG, PNG and WebP. Convert iPhone photos in HEIC format to JPG first.

faq.q: Do my photos stay on my device?
faq.a: Yes. Everything runs in the browser: files are not uploaded to a server and are not stored.

photoToPdf.title: Why combine photos into a single PDF file
photoToPdf.text1: PDF remains the universal format for sending documents: it opens the same way on a computer, a phone, or inside an email client, and its pages don't get scattered the way separate photos do in a chat. A PDF is easy to attach to an email, print, or upload to a portal that accepts only one document instead of a dozen separate images. People most often combine scanned documents, photographed notebook or book pages, receipts for an expense report, or product photos for a catalog into one PDF.
photoToPdf.text2: This tool combines several photos into one PDF right in your browser: add the files, arrange them in the order you need, choose a page size and margins, and download the finished document. Photos are never uploaded to a server or stored anywhere.

benefits.title: Page order under your control
benefits.text: Use the ↑↓ arrows or drag photos into the order they should appear in the document.

benefits.title: No quality loss where possible
benefits.text: An unrotated JPEG and a plain PNG are embedded into the PDF as they are, without re-compression.

benefits.title: Nothing uploaded to a server
benefits.text: The whole PDF is built in your browser; the files never leave your device.

benefits.title: Flexible page sizes
benefits.text: A4 with margins for printing, or a page sized to match the photo when you need the exact shot dimensions.

sections.title: How to combine photos into a PDF
steps: Drag photos into the upload area or click it and choose files. JPEG, PNG, WebP, BMP, GIF, AVIF and HEIC/HEIF (iPhone photos) are all supported.
Arrange the photos in the order you need: use the ↑↓ arrows next to each file or drag them in the list.
Choose the page size and margins in the settings above the upload area.
Click "Create PDF" and download the finished file once it's ready.

sections.title: Page size: A4 or photo size
sections.text: An A4 page suits printing and documents expected in a standard size: each photo is fitted onto the sheet while keeping its proportions, and the orientation (portrait or landscape) is chosen automatically from the shape of the photo itself. "Photo size" makes the page exactly the size of the image (plus margins, if enabled) — handy when it matters to keep the original proportions without adding white bars around the shot.

sections.title: Page margins
sections.text: A 0 mm margin means the photo fills almost the entire page. A 10 mm margin adds a small border on every side, similar to most office documents — useful if the PDF will be printed or filed.

sections.title: How quality is preserved
sections.text: For a JPEG without a rotation tag and for a plain PNG, the tool embeds the original image bytes into the PDF — with no re-compression or re-encoding. If a JPEG carries a rotation tag (typical for portrait photos from smartphones) or the format isn't supported directly (WebP, BMP, GIF, AVIF, HEIC/HEIF), the photo is first corrected to the right orientation and re-encoded as JPEG at 92% quality, the same way other tools on the site do it. In both cases PNG transparency is filled with white, since a printed page has no transparency.

sections.title: Limits worth knowing about
sections.text: The limit is 30 MB per file and up to 20 files at once; if the whole album is over 200 MB, a warning appears but processing still finishes. Very large photos or a large number of pages can produce a heavy PDF and take longer on slower devices. The tool doesn't add page numbers, watermarks, or captions — just the photos themselves, one per page.

sections.title: Privacy
sections.text: The whole PDF is assembled locally in your browser. Photos are never sent to a server, never stored, and never accessible to us; once you close the page, nothing remains except the file you downloaded to your device.

faq.q: Can I change the photo order after adding files?
faq.a: Yes. As long as the PDF hasn't been created yet, you can reorder photos with the ↑↓ arrows next to each file or by dragging them in the list.

faq.q: Does the photo quality get worse in the PDF?
faq.a: An unrotated JPEG and a plain PNG are embedded without re-encoding. Rotated photos and formats like WebP or HEIC are re-encoded as JPEG at 92% quality to keep the correct orientation.

faq.q: Which page size should I choose?
faq.a: A4 for printing or documents expected in a standard size; "photo size" when you need to keep the original shot proportions without white margins around it.

faq.q: How many photos can I add?
faq.a: Up to 20 files at once, up to 30 MB each. If the total size is over 200 MB, a warning appears, but processing still completes.

faq.q: Can I add just one photo?
faq.a: Yes, you'll get a one-page PDF — useful, for example, to send a photo of a document as a PDF.

faq.q: Do my photos stay on a server?
faq.a: No. The PDF is built in your browser; the files are never uploaded anywhere.

cropImage.title: Why crop a photo online
cropImage.text1: Cropping is one of the simplest ways to improve a photo: trim distracting edges, draw attention to the subject, or fit the shot to a specific ratio — a square for a profile picture, a wide frame for a cover image, or a vertical crop for a Story. People most often crop before posting to Instagram, Facebook, or YouTube, for an avatar or a website banner, or simply to cut out people or objects at the edge of the frame.
cropImage.text2: This tool lets you crop a photo right in your browser: drag the selection frame or its corners with a mouse or a finger, pick a ready-made ratio from the list or leave it freeform, then download the result as JPG, PNG, or WebP. The photo is never uploaded to a server and isn't stored anywhere.

benefits.title: Precise selection frame
benefits.text: Drag the whole frame or just one corner with a mouse or a finger and see the result update instantly on the photo itself — no guessing and no repeated attempts.

benefits.title: Ready-made social ratios
benefits.text: 1:1 for a profile picture, 9:16 for Stories and Reels, 16:9 for a video cover — plus the other common ratios, or a freeform frame when you need an exact custom shape.

benefits.title: No quality loss
benefits.text: Cropping just selects part of the image rather than compressing it: the pixels inside the frame stay exactly as sharp as the original. You choose the output format and compression yourself.

benefits.title: Nothing is uploaded
benefits.text: The whole crop happens in your browser, on your own device; the photo is never sent anywhere or stored.

sections.title: How to crop a photo
steps: Drag a photo into the upload area or click it and choose a file. JPEG, PNG, WebP, BMP, GIF, AVIF, and HEIC/HEIF (iPhone photos) are all supported.
Pick a ready-made ratio in the settings, or leave it on “Free” for a custom shape.
Drag the frame to move the selection, or its corners to resize it.
Choose the output format (JPG, PNG, or WebP) and click “Crop & Download”.

sections.title: Ready-made ratios and freeform selection
sections.text: The ratio list covers the most common cases: a 1:1 square for avatars and social profiles, 4:3 and 3:2 for classic photo framing, and 16:9 and 9:16 for video and vertical Stories — each available in both orientations. If none of them fit, pick “Free” and drag the corners to set any shape you need.

sections.title: Output formats: JPG, PNG, WebP
sections.text: The output format is separate from the format of the file you uploaded. JPG suits photos and gives the smallest file size; PNG keeps transparency if the original had it; WebP combines a small size with transparency support, though it isn't supported by every older app.

sections.title: Does cropping reduce quality
sections.text: Cropping itself doesn't touch the pixels inside the selected area — they stay exactly as sharp as in the original. Some loss is only possible during the final encoding to JPG or WebP (lossy formats), the same as saving any photo in those formats; PNG encodes without any loss at all.

sections.title: Supported upload formats
sections.text: The tool accepts JPEG, PNG, WebP, BMP, GIF, AVIF, and HEIC/HEIF — the format iPhones save photos in by default. Whatever the source format, you can always save the result as JPG, PNG, or WebP.

sections.title: Privacy
sections.text: The photo is processed entirely in your browser: it is never uploaded to a server, stored, or sent anywhere, even temporarily. Close the tab and every trace of the file is gone.

faq.q: Can I crop a photo on my phone?
faq.a: Yes — you can drag the frame and its corners with a finger just like with a mouse on a computer; the interface is built for touch screens.

faq.q: Can I crop a photo into a circle?
faq.a: Right now the selection frame is rectangular only. A circular crop could be a separate tool down the line.

faq.q: Will cropping reduce the quality?
faq.a: The pixels inside the frame aren't changed by the crop itself. Some loss is possible only when saving as JPG or WebP, which are lossy formats — pick PNG if you need a crop with absolutely no loss.

faq.q: How many photos can I crop in a row?
faq.a: As many as you like — the tool handles one photo at a time: just upload the next one right after downloading the previous result.

faq.q: Which photo formats are supported?
faq.a: On upload: JPEG, PNG, WebP, BMP, GIF, AVIF, and HEIC/HEIF. You can save the result as JPG, PNG, or WebP.

faq.q: Is there a file size limit?
faq.a: Yes, up to 30 MB per file — plenty for photos from any modern phone or camera.

rotateImage.title: Why rotate or flip a photo online
rotateImage.text1: A photo from a phone or camera sometimes ends up sideways or upside down — the camera got the orientation wrong while shooting, or the file is opened in an app that ignores the rotation tag. Rotating such a shot by 90°, 180°, or the other way is one of the simplest fixes that noticeably improves how a photo reads. Flipping (a horizontal or vertical mirror) is useful for something different: fixing "backwards" text captured through a mirror or shop window, turning a portrait so the subject's gaze points toward text in a layout, or just picking whichever composition looks more natural.
rotateImage.text2: This tool rotates and flips photos right in your browser: upload a photo, click the rotate or flip buttons — the preview updates instantly, so you see the result right away. Once the orientation looks right, download the file as JPG, PNG, or WebP. Nothing gets uploaded to a server or stored anywhere.

benefits.title: Instant result
benefits.text: Rotation and flipping apply the moment you click a button — no processing wait, the preview updates in real time.

benefits.title: Rotate and flip together
benefits.text: Combine both actions in any order and any number of times — for example, rotate 90° and also flip horizontally — to land on exactly the orientation you need.

benefits.title: No quality loss at 90°/180°
benefits.text: Rotating by 90°, 180°, or 270° and flipping only move the same pixels around rather than recalculating them, so image sharpness stays the same.

benefits.title: Nothing uploaded to a server
benefits.text: All processing happens right in your browser on your own device; the photo is never sent anywhere or stored on our side.

sections.title: How to rotate or flip a photo
steps: Drag a photo into the upload area, or click it to choose a file. JPEG, PNG, WebP, BMP, GIF, AVIF, and HEIC/HEIF (iPhone photos) are all supported.
Click "Left 90°" or "Right 90°" to rotate the photo — the preview updates instantly; clicking one twice in a row gives you a 180° rotation.
If needed, turn on a horizontal or vertical flip — the toggle buttons can be combined with rotation in any way.
Pick the output format (JPG, PNG, or WebP) and click "Download".

sections.title: 90°, 180° rotation and flipping
sections.text: The "Left 90°" and "Right 90°" buttons turn the image a quarter turn in the chosen direction; clicking one twice gives a 180° rotation. A horizontal flip mirrors the photo left-right, a vertical flip mirrors it top-bottom; both flags are independent of rotation and can be switched on at the same time as it, so any orientation you need is a few clicks away.

sections.title: Output formats: JPG, PNG, WebP
sections.text: Choose the result format independently of the source file's format. JPG suits photographs and gives the smallest file size; PNG keeps transparency if the original had any; WebP combines a small size with transparency support, though it doesn't open in every older program.

sections.title: Does rotating hurt image quality
sections.text: Rotating by 90°, 180°, or 270° and flipping only rearrange pixels without recalculating or blending them, so sharpness stays exactly the same as the original. Some loss is possible only during the final encode to JPG or WebP (lossy formats), the same as saving any photo in those formats; PNG encodes losslessly.

sections.title: Privacy
sections.text: The photo is processed entirely in your browser: it is never uploaded to a server, never stored, and never transmitted anywhere, even temporarily. Close the tab and every trace of the work is gone.

faq.q: Can I rotate a photo by an arbitrary angle, not just 90°?
faq.a: Right now only 90° steps (and their combinations up to 270°) plus flipping are available. Arbitrary-angle rotation could be a separate tool down the line.

faq.q: What's the difference between rotating and flipping?
faq.a: Rotating turns the whole image around its center by 90°, 180°, or 270°. Flipping mirrors the photo along one axis — left-right (horizontal) or top-bottom (vertical) — without turning it.

faq.q: Will rotating reduce photo quality?
faq.a: No, rotating by 90°, 180°, or 270° and flipping only rearrange pixels. Some loss is possible only when saving as JPG or WebP — lossy formats; pick PNG if you need it completely lossless.

faq.q: Can I rotate and flip a photo at the same time?
faq.a: Yes, the two actions are independent: rotate first and flip after (or the other way around), and undo or repeat either one at any point — the preview always shows the current result.

faq.q: Which photo formats are supported?
faq.a: On input: JPEG, PNG, WebP, BMP, GIF, AVIF, and HEIC/HEIF. The result can be saved as JPG, PNG, or WebP.

faq.q: Is there a file size limit?
faq.a: Yes, up to 30 MB per file — plenty for photos from any modern phone or camera.

addWatermark.title: Why add a watermark to a photo
addWatermark.text1: A watermark — a caption or logo laid over a photo — protects original photos from being used without permission while also reminding the viewer where the image came from. Photographers stamp a signature or studio name on a portfolio before posting to social media; marketplace sellers add a logo to product photos so competitors can't copy them; bloggers brand screenshots and video stills with their own mark. A bold caption across the center scares off casual theft entirely, while a subtle mark in a corner or a barely-visible overlay keeps the photo looking clean while still being legally marked.
addWatermark.text2: This tool adds a text watermark or your own logo to a photo right in your browser: type a caption or upload an image, pick a position — one of four corners, the center, or a repeating "tile" pattern across the whole frame — and adjust size and opacity. The preview updates instantly, so you see the result before downloading. The finished file saves as JPG, PNG, or WebP; nothing gets uploaded to a server or stored anywhere.

benefits.title: Text or your own logo
benefits.text: Type a caption or upload an image of your logo — both work with the same position, size, and opacity controls.

benefits.title: One mark or a full tiled pattern
benefits.text: A single watermark in a corner or center protects less than a repeating tile across the whole photo — a tiled pattern is much harder to crop out.

benefits.title: Live preview
benefits.text: Every change to text, color, size, opacity, or position shows up instantly in the preview — no guessing how it'll look after downloading.

benefits.title: Nothing uploaded to a server
benefits.text: All processing happens right in your browser on your own device; the photo and logo are never sent anywhere or stored on our side.

sections.title: How to add a watermark to a photo
steps: Drag a photo into the upload area, or click it to choose a file. JPEG, PNG, WebP, BMP, GIF, AVIF, and HEIC/HEIF (iPhone photos) are all supported.
Pick the watermark type — text or image (upload a logo file with its own button).
Adjust size, color (for text), and opacity — the preview updates instantly.
Choose a position — one of four corners, the center, or "Tile" — and the output format, then click "Download".

sections.title: Text watermark or logo
sections.text: A text watermark suits cases where a name, caption, or short link is enough — just type the text and pick a color and font size. A logo makes the brand clearer: upload a PNG with a transparent background for the cleanest result (no white box around the mark), or any other format such as a photo or screenshot. Both scale relative to the photo's own size, so they look proportional on both small and large images.

sections.title: Position and tiling
sections.text: The five fixed positions — four corners and center — suit a soft, barely-noticeable caption that doesn't get in the way of viewing the photo. "Tile" mode repeats the watermark across the whole frame at even intervals — the most reliable protection against theft, since no part of the photo can be cropped away without losing the mark, though it's more noticeable.

sections.title: Opacity and size
sections.text: Opacity ranges from 5% (barely visible) to 100% (solid and clearly readable). Font or logo size is calculated as a percentage of the photo's own dimensions, so proportions stay consistent whether you upload an 800×600 shot or a 6000×4000 one.

sections.title: Output formats: JPG, PNG, WebP
sections.text: Choose the result format independently of the source file's format. JPG suits photographs and gives the smallest file size; PNG keeps transparency if the original had any; WebP combines a small size with transparency support, though it doesn't open in every older program.

sections.title: Privacy
sections.text: The photo and logo are processed entirely in your browser: neither is ever uploaded to a server, stored, or transmitted anywhere, even temporarily. Close the tab and every trace of the work is gone.

faq.q: Can I make the watermark nearly invisible?
faq.a: Yes, the opacity slider goes down to 5% — the mark stays embedded in the file but is barely noticeable.

faq.q: Can I use my own logo instead of text?
faq.a: Yes, pick the "Image" type and upload a logo file — a PNG with a transparent background works best, so there's no white box around the mark.

faq.q: What does "Tile" mode do?
faq.a: The watermark repeats across the whole photo at even intervals instead of a single caption in one corner — a much stronger deterrent against cropping or retouching the mark out.

faq.q: Will adding a watermark reduce photo quality?
faq.a: Applying the mark itself doesn't change the rest of the image. Some loss is possible only when saving as JPG or WebP — lossy formats; pick PNG if you need it completely lossless.

faq.q: Which photo formats are supported?
faq.a: On input: JPEG, PNG, WebP, BMP, GIF, AVIF, and HEIC/HEIF. The result can be saved as JPG, PNG, or WebP.

faq.q: Is there a file size limit?
faq.a: Yes, up to 30 MB per file — plenty for photos from any modern phone or camera.
